title: A recursive call of a function whose optional argument has a default that allocates locally is not a tail call
summary: A function with an optional argument whose default allocates on the local stack (here a comparison of two tuples) does not call itself in constant stack in native code. A loop written so ends with `Stack_overflow`; bytecode and OCaml 5.4.0 run it in constant stack.
cause: `split_default_wrapper` in `lambda/simplif.ml` keeps a region in the wrapper when a default may allocate locally, and calls the inner function with `Rc_normal`, so the region is ended after that call returns.

fix.text: Ends the region of the wrapper before its call of the inner function when no parameter is local. Builds; `test.ml` then prints the expected result; testsuite unchanged.

reference: related: issues #7724 and #4797 (the wrapper allocating; not the same)
